title: SPREAD Annual Report 2023–2024
source_family: SPREAD implementing-organisation reports; not independent of 2024–25 report
inspection: 24-page PDF recovered; cover and printed pages 14–16 (PDF pages 15–17) visually inspected in full; relevant text read.

findings.claim: Folkweave programme includes natural dyeing, weaving and stitching; group training and Samartha stipend provision described.
findings.limit: Not identified as a Dongria embroidery payment ledger.

findings.claim: Niru, identified as Rana, reportedly received Rs 14,000 for 45 days of weaving training and subsequently Rs 3,000 monthly for part-time weaving and dyeing.
findings.limit: Organisation-reported historical account, not Dongria Kapadaganda earnings or audited net income.

findings.claim: Ani, described only as from a tribal community, reportedly earned Rs 3,000 monthly for part-time dyeing and stitching.
findings.limit: No Dongria identity or Kapadaganda work specified; no inference from photographs or generic tribal designation.

not_adopted: Programme-wide income-increase percentage as a Dongria outcome
Group sizes as Dongria participant counts
Natural-dye programme as proof of Kapadaganda thread dye or base-cloth supply
Unverified generic search-result wage and organic-cotton claims
article_decision: No article change. Existing article already separates programme sales from maker payments; recovered earlier report does not close individual Dongria payment gap.
next_evidence: Dated maker- or group-linked Kapadaganda purchase/commission record with quantities, payments, materials supplied and costs borne, or clearly attributed participant account.
